correctness.rationale: For char!=2, S=A+At with t=x/z, t^2=z^2-y^2z, and R=A+ztA. Singular gradient of t^2+y^2z-z^2 vanishes only at origin; hypersurface S2+R1 gives normality. Completing square u=z-y^2/2 yields t^2-u^2+y^4/4, type A3. S/R=A/(z) and conductor zS=(z,x). In char2 w=x+z^2 has w^2=y^2z^3; R is domain because z-adic valuation 3 prevents a square in k(y,z). t=w/(yz) obeys t^2=z; S=k[y,t]=A+At, R=A+yztA, same fraction field, finite/birational and normal; conductor yz S=(yz,w), quotient A/(yz). F_z=y^2z^2, leading to reduced support V(x,z) union V(y,x+z^2), and z=t^2 on the latter is purely inseparable degree2. The script confirms polynomial identities but proof uses ring structure.
